## Prerequisites

- Docker (or Docker Desktop)
- Git (or GitHub Desktop)

## Quick start

**1. Clone the PaleoPAL repository**

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/LinkedEarth/PaleoPAL.git
cd PaleoPAL
```

**2. Create the environment file**

```bash
# Create environment file
cp backend/env.example backend/.env
```

**3. Add your API keys**

You need to add you API keys to the `backend/.env` file. You can do so with any text editor.

```
# Edit backend/.env with your API keys:
# OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_key_here
# GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_key_here
# XAI_API_KEY=your_key_here
```

Instructions on how to obtain API keys vary by providers:  
- OPEN AI API key can be obtained from the [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/).  
- ANTHROPIC API key can be obtained from the [Anthropic Platform](https://console.anthropic.com/).  
- GOOGLE API key can be obtained from the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/).  
- XAI API key can be obtained from the [XAI Platform](https://x.ai/).    


**4. Start all services**

```bash
# Start all services
docker compose up -d
```

Using `-d` (or `--detach`) runs your containers in the background, allowing you to continue using the terminal while the services are running.

**5. Access the application**

Once running, the services are available at:

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Frontend | <http://localhost:3000> |
| Backend API | <http://localhost:8000> |
| Qdrant Dashboard | <http://localhost:6333/dashboard> |

**6. Populating the knowledge base** [Optional after first use]

The first time you are using PaleoPAL, you need to populate the knowledge base with relevant data.

***a. Download the notebook resources***

Most sources are already available in the repository, but you need to download the notebook resources separately and index them. 

::: {.callout-note}
Although you may theoretically use any notebook to populate the knowledge base, it is recommended to use the provided notebooks for best results. These notebooks are designed to work with the code knowledge embedded in PaleoPAL. We cannot guarantee the accuracy of results when using notebook calling software libraries not indexed in the knowledge base.
::: 


```bash
# Set environment variables
export QDRANT_HOST=localhost
export QDRANT_PORT=6333

# Run the indexing script
cd backend/libraries
bash index_everything.sh
```

This indexes SPARQL queries, ontology entities, notebook snippets and workflows, ReadTheDocs documentation, and literature methods.

::: {.callout-note}
If using `docker-compose`, either set `export QDRANT_PORT=6333` on the host before indexing, or run indexing from within a container that can reach `qdrant:6333`. The first run downloads the embedding model — allow a few minutes.
:::
